title: TickTockRatificationProposal/1.0
description: The artifact a REFUSED charter-or-meta-file edit must produce. SKILL.md (tt.improve) hard-blocks a candidate touching the charter, .claude/skills/go/, .claude/skills/meditate/, .claude/skills/ticktock/, instructions/canonical/dispatch-routing-rule.yaml, or the capabilities matrix -- and says the refusal must EMIT this proposal rather than stop: 'a bare refusal is an incomplete outcome (this is what S3-c checks)'. A refusal tells the cycle what it may not do; this artifact tells the operator what could be ratified instead, which is the difference between a wall and a door. It is a PROPOSAL: writing it changes nothing, ratifies nothing, and never itself edits the blocked target. The operator is the gate.

proposal_id.description: tt-proposal-<UTC timestamp>-<8 hex of the target+change digest>. Also the filename stem. The digest suffix means two proposals raised in the same second against different targets cannot collide.

charter_hash.description: The charter in force when the edit was refused. A proposal does not carry across charters.

refusal.description: The refusal this proposal is the completion of. halt_state uses the journal's halt vocabulary so a proposal and a journal record never disagree about why the edit was blocked.

refused_by.description: The mechanism that refused -- e.g. charter.checkImmutability, or the allowed_write_surfaces bound.

kind.description: What class of protected surface was targeted. 'other' exists so an unanticipated refusal is still recordable rather than silently unrecordable.

inside_allowed_write_surfaces.description: Whether the target sits inside the charter's own allowed_write_surfaces. False is the ordinary case for a meta-file: the charter's bound is the mechanism that refused.

proposed_change.description: WHAT was wanted, described rather than applied. There is deliberately no field here that an executor could replay: a proposal that could be auto-applied would be an edit wearing a proposal's name.

fields.description: The specific fields or sections the change would touch, with their current and wanted values rendered as strings.

diff_preview.description: Human-readable rendering of the change. Never machine-applied.

rationale.description: The same four things every /tt improvement candidate carries. A proposal with no falsifier is a preference, and is marked as one by leaving falsifier empty -- the field is required so the absence is visible.

ratification_path.description: The route from this proposal to a ratified change. The producer never walks it; it names it.

decided_by.description: Who may ratify. Never the cycle that raised the proposal -- a producer never validates its own trial.

status.description: The only value this producer may write. Ratification, rejection, and withdrawal are the operator's edits to make, not the cycle's.

proposal_hash.description: sha256 over the canonical projection with proposal_hash omitted. Computed by the writer; a caller-supplied hash is recomputed and must match.
